chapters.title: Working on a ticket
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who handle tickets day to day.

It explains the ticket screen, statuses and service targets. It shows how to assign, resolve, escalate, merge and link tickets. It also covers tasks, time, watchers, follow-ups and what automation does on your tickets.

sections.title: Open a ticket
sections.intro: Open a ticket from a list, or go straight to it by its number.
steps: In the ticket list, select the ticket's row.
To open a ticket by number, press [[Ctrl+K]] and enter the number, such as `1042`.
Select the ticket in the results.
sections.result: The ticket opens in its own tab in the ticket workspace.

blocks.note: If the ticket is deleted, merged or outside what you can see, **Ticket not found** appears. Select **Close tab** to close it. See also [Find a ticket from the command palette](#gs-find-ticket).

sections.title: The ticket screen
intro: The ticket screen has a header, the conversation and the composer. The customer's context pane is on the right.
On most laptop screens, the side tabs open in a **Ticket details** panel. On wide screens, they appear next to the conversation.

blocks.caption: Ticket #1002 with the header, the conversation, the composer bar and the context pane.
blocks.alt: Ticket screen with numbered highlights on the ticket number, facts, quick edit fields, Ticket details button, More actions button, conversation header, composer bar and the customer section

callouts: The ticket number. Select it to copy a link to the ticket. The subject and the **Edit subject** button are next to it.
Facts: channel, customer, contact, badges and the service target countdowns.
**Ticket details**: opens the side tabs, such as **Details**, **Tasks**, **Time** and **People**.
**More actions**: assign, transfer, escalate, resolve, merge and the other ticket actions.
The conversation, with the **Activity** switch and the **Expand all** and **Collapse all** buttons.
The context pane, starting with the customer.

blocks.tip: To give the ticket more room, select the panel buttons at either end of the tab strip. They hide the queue panel and the context pane.

sections.title: Badges in the ticket header
sections.intro: Badges under the subject tell you about the ticket at a glance.

rows: The ticket is escalated. The number is the escalation level.
A contract covers the request. Point to the badge to see the contract.
No valid contract covers the request.
Someone allowed support although the customer is not entitled.
The ticket is resolved, and SupportDesk waits for the customer to confirm the fix.
Another person locked the ticket while they work on it.
This ticket was merged into another. Select the badge to open the other ticket.
Shown on resolved and closed tickets instead of countdowns.

sections.title: The conversation
intro: The conversation shows every message on the ticket, oldest first. The newest entry is at the bottom.
Customer messages and replies show the channel, such as **wrote via WhatsApp**. Internal notes and handover notes have an amber background. Customers never see them.

list: Turn on **Activity** to also see field changes, routing, SLA events and automation.
Select **Expand all** or **Collapse all** to open or fold every message. Long older messages start folded.
E-mail messages show **From**, **To** and **Cc** above the text.
Replies show a delivery status, such as **Delivered**.
Select an attachment to download it. **Scanning** means the malware scan is still running. **Blocked** means the file failed the scan.

blocks.note: If the description is not part of the conversation, it appears in a box above the conversation.

sections.title: The context pane
sections.intro: The context pane on the right shows what you need to know about the customer. Select a section heading to fold or unfold it.

rows: Name, tier, account manager, open tickets, tickets in 90 days, satisfaction score and breaches. **Open customer** opens the customer's page.
Job title, location, e-mail address, phone, language, preferred channel and open tickets.
Each service target with its status, due time and target. See [Service targets](#wt-sla).
The customer's contracts. **Covers** marks the one that covers this ticket. Prepaid contracts show the hours used.
The customer's installed products, with versions.
The customer's earlier tickets. Select one to open it.
Related documents in the ERP system, such as invoices.
Knowledge base articles that match the ticket, with a match score.
Suggestions from the AI assistant, with a confidence level.
Linked engineering work items and their state.

sections.title: Change fields from the header
sections.intro: Use the quick edit fields to change the most common fields without opening a dialog.
prerequisites: The fields you may change depend on your permissions. Fields you cannot change are greyed out.
steps: To change the subject, select **Edit subject** (the pencil). Enter the new subject and select **Save**.
To change the status, choose a status in **Status**.
To change the priority, choose it in **Priority**.
To assign the ticket, choose an agent in **Assignee**. Select **Assign to me** next to it to take the ticket yourself.
To move the ticket, choose another **Department** or **Team**.
sections.result: Each change saves at once. A message confirms it, such as **Priority set to High**.

blocks.warning: Quick edit fields save as soon as you choose a value. There is no **Save** button.

blocks.note: Some departments need a supervisor's approval for transfers. Then the message **Approval requested** appears, and the ticket stays where it is until someone approves.

sections.title: Ticket statuses
intro: Every status belongs to one fixed category: Open, Assigned, In progress, Waiting, Resolved or Closed. New workspaces start with the statuses below.
Your administrator can add statuses and limit which status may follow which. The status list only offers the statuses allowed next.

rows: A new ticket. The customer portal shows **Received**.
Assign it, reply, or change the status.
Set automatically when an open ticket gets an assignee.
Reply. Your reply moves the ticket to **In Progress**.
Set automatically when an agent replies to an open or assigned ticket.
Keep working, wait for someone, or resolve.
You asked the customer for something. The service clock pauses. Sub-statuses: information requested, confirmation requested, scheduling.
Wait. A customer reply moves the ticket back to **In Progress**, or to **Open** when nobody owns it.
You wait for engineering, a vendor or a partner. The clock keeps running. Sub-statuses: engineering, vendor, partner.
Follow up with the third party. A customer reply moves the ticket back as above.
An example status in the demo workspace. The ticket waits for an engineering fix.
Follow the work item in the context pane.
The fix is delivered. The ticket closes itself after a set number of days. The standard is 7 days.
Close it, or reopen it. A customer reply reopens it.
Reopen it. A customer reply within the reopen window also reopens it.

blocks.note: Some fields can be required for a status. For example, a vendor reference while the ticket waits on a third party. Fill them in on the **Details** tab before you change the status.
Tickets that follow a blueprint cannot change status freely. Use the **Blueprint** tab instead. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).

sections.title: Change the status with a comment
sections.intro: Use the **Change status** dialog when you want to add a sub-status or a comment.
steps: Press [[S]], or open **More actions** and choose **Change status…**.

steps.caption: The **Change status** dialog with **Waiting on Customer** chosen. A **Sub-status** list appears.
steps.alt: Change status dialog with Status, Sub-status and Comment fields

steps: If **Sub-status** appears, choose one.
In **Comment**, enter a short note for the ticket history.
Select **Change status**.
sections.result: The status changes. The message **Status changed to** and the status name appears.

sections.title: Service targets
intro: A service level agreement (SLA) sets time targets for each ticket. The header shows a countdown for each target that is still running.
**First response** shows until someone replies. After that, **Next response** shows the time for the next reply. **Resolve** shows the time left to resolve the ticket.

rows: At risk. The ticket passed the warning point, normally 75% of the target.
The ticket is in a status that pauses the clock, such as **Waiting on Customer**.

blocks.caption: The SLA section of the context pane: the first response was met, the other two targets were breached.
blocks.alt: SLA section listing First response as Met, and Next response and Resolution as Breached, each with a due time and target

blocks.p: The SLA section of the context pane shows the true state of each target. It also shows the due time, the target in minutes and the escalation level.

blocks.note: The header countdowns use the ticket's overall SLA state. After one target is breached, every countdown in the header turns red. The first response clock never pauses.

sections.title: Assign a ticket
sections.intro: Give the ticket to an agent or a team. To take it yourself, press [[A]].
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Assign…**.

steps.text: In **Team**, choose a team, or leave it empty.
steps.caption: The **Assign ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Assign ticket dialog with Team, Agent, an Assign to me link and Note

steps: In **Agent**, choose an agent of the ticket's department. Select **Assign to me** to choose yourself.
In **Note**, enter a note for the ticket history if you like.
Select **Assign**.
sections.result: The message **Assigned to** and the agent's name appears. An open ticket moves to **Assigned**.

blocks.note: Leave **Agent** empty to unassign the ticket. The agent list shows each agent's availability and open tickets.

sections.title: Transfer a ticket to another department
sections.intro: Move a ticket to another department's queue when another team must handle it.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Transfer…**.

steps.caption: The **Transfer ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Transfer ticket dialog with Department, Team, Agent and Reason fields

steps: In **Team** and **Agent**, choose who should get it. Leave **Agent** empty to let routing pick an agent.
In **Reason**, say why you transfer the ticket.
Select **Transfer**.
sections.result: The message **Transferred to** and the department's name appears.

blocks.note: Some departments need a supervisor's approval first. Then **Approval requested** appears. The ticket moves when the request is approved on the **Approvals** page.

sections.title: Resolve a ticket
sections.intro: Resolve a ticket when you have delivered the fix or the answer.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Resolve…**.

steps.text: In **Resolution code**, choose how the problem was solved.
steps.caption: The **Resolve ticket** dialog.
steps.alt: Resolve ticket dialog with Resolution code, Root cause, Resolution notes and two check boxes

steps: In **Root cause**, choose or enter the cause.
In **Resolution notes**, describe the fix. The customer sees these notes when you notify them.
Keep **Notify the customer** ticked to send the resolution notice and the satisfaction survey.
Tick **Ask the customer to confirm the fix (keeps it open until they reply)** if the customer must confirm.
Select **Resolve**.
sections.result: The status changes to **Resolved**. With the confirmation option, the header shows **Awaiting customer confirmation**.

blocks.note: **Resolution code** is required when your workspace uses codes. The confirmation option needs a contact on the ticket. Your workspace may switch it on for every ticket.

blocks.p: Resolved tickets close themselves after the number of days your administrator sets. A customer reply before then reopens the ticket.

sections.title: Close or reopen a ticket
sections.intro: Close a ticket when the work is finished. Reopen it when the problem comes back.
prerequisites: Closing needs the resolve permission. Reopening needs the reopen permission.
steps: To close the ticket, open **More actions** and choose **Close**.
Select **Close ticket** to confirm.
To reopen a resolved or closed ticket, open **More actions** and choose **Reopen…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, say why you reopen it.
steps.caption: The **Reopen ticket** dialog on a closed ticket.
steps.alt: Reopen ticket dialog with a Reason box

steps: Select **Reopen**.
sections.result: A closed ticket shows **Closed**. A reopened ticket gets an open status, the service clocks restart, and the reopen count goes up.

blocks.note: A customer reply also reopens a closed ticket within the reopen window. The standard window is 30 days. After it, the reply becomes a new ticket. Merged tickets cannot be reopened.

sections.title: Escalate a ticket
sections.intro: Escalate a ticket when it needs more senior attention. Each escalation raises the escalation level by one.
steps: Press [[E]], or open **More actions** and choose **Escalate…**.

steps.text: In **Reason**, say why the ticket needs escalating.
steps.caption: The **Escalate ticket** dialog with a reason.
steps.alt: Escalate ticket dialog with Reason, Escalate to and a Raise the priority one level check box

steps: In **Escalate to**, choose a person, or leave it empty for the department's escalation owner.
Keep **Raise the priority one level** ticked to raise the priority too.
Select **Escalate**.
sections.result: The header shows the **Escalated** badge with the new level. The escalation owner is notified.

blocks.note: On a ticket that is already escalated, the menu item reads **Escalate further…**. The person you choose in **Escalate to** also becomes a watcher.

sections.title: Merge duplicate tickets
sections.intro: When a customer reports the same problem twice, merge the duplicates into one ticket.
prerequisites: Open the ticket you want to keep.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Merge tickets into this…**.
In **Find tickets**, enter a number, subject, customer or contact.

steps.text: Choose a duplicate in the results. Repeat for up to 10 tickets.
steps.caption: The **Merge tickets** dialog with ticket #1204 picked as a duplicate.
steps.alt: Merge tickets dialog with a search box, one picked ticket and a Note field

steps: In **Note**, say why you merge the tickets if you like.
Select **Merge** followed by the number of tickets.
sections.result: The conversation, attachments, time, watchers, tags and engineering links move to this ticket. The duplicates close with a link to this ticket.

blocks.warning: You cannot undo a merge. Merged tickets cannot be reopened.

blocks.tip: Select **×** next to a picked ticket to remove it from the merge.

sections.title: Split messages into a new ticket
sections.intro: When one ticket mixes two problems, move some messages to a new ticket for the same customer.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Split messages…**.
Check the **New subject**. Change it to describe the second problem.

steps.text: Under **Messages**, tick each message to move.
steps.caption: The **Split into a new ticket** dialog with the first customer message ticked.
steps.alt: Split dialog with a New subject field, a list of messages with check boxes and a child ticket option

steps: Keep **Link the new ticket as a child of this one** ticked to link the two tickets.
Select **Split**.
sections.result: The new ticket opens in a new tab. The message **Created** and the new number appears.

sections.title: Clone a ticket
sections.intro: Clone a ticket to start a similar one for the same customer.
prerequisites: You need the create tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Clone**.

steps.caption: The confirmation before cloning ticket #1002.
steps.alt: Clone confirmation dialog with Cancel and Clone buttons

sections.result: The new ticket opens in a new tab. It has the same customer, fields, tags and description. It does not copy the conversation.

sections.title: Link related tickets
sections.intro: Link tickets that belong together, such as a ticket that blocks another.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Link to ticket…**.
In **Relationship**, choose **Related to**, **Duplicate of**, **Blocks** or **Caused by**.

steps.text: In **Ticket**, search for the other ticket and choose it.
steps.caption: The **Link ticket** dialog linking #1002 as a duplicate of #1204.
steps.alt: Link ticket dialog with a Relationship list and a Ticket search box

steps: Select **Link**.
sections.result: The message **Tickets linked** appears. The **Related** tab of both tickets shows the link.

blocks.caption: The **Related** tab of a ticket without related tickets.
blocks.alt: Related tab with Child tickets, Linked tickets with a Link button, and External references

blocks.p: The **Related** tab also lists the parent ticket, child tickets and external references, such as ERP documents. To remove a link, select **×** next to it.

sections.title: Edit tags, classification and custom fields
sections.intro: Keep the ticket's classification up to date. Reports, routing and service targets use it.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details** (the sliders button in the header).

steps.caption: The **Details** tab in the **Ticket details** panel.
steps.alt: Details tab with Tags, Category, Subcategory, Issue type, Severity, Product, Module, Version and Installation

steps: In **Tags**, type a tag and press [[Enter]]. Select **×** on a tag to remove it.
Change the classification and product fields you need.
Fill in the fields under **Additional fields**.
Select **Save**.
sections.result: The message **Ticket updated** appears. The bar at the bottom shows **All changes saved**.

blocks.note: Tags save at once. The other fields wait for **Save**. Select **Undo** to drop changes you have not saved.

blocks.p: **Installation** needs a customer on the ticket. **Subcategory** needs a category, and **Module** and **Version** need a product.
The **Facts** list shows the dates, the SLA policy and the contract. It also shows the time spent, the reopen count, the satisfaction score and the resolution.

sections.title: Add tasks and checklist items
sections.intro: Break the work into tasks, each with an owner and a due time.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets or the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Tasks** tab.

steps.text: In **New task or checklist item**, enter what needs doing.
steps.caption: The **Tasks** tab with a new task typed in.
steps.alt: Tasks tab with a task title, Assignee, a due date and time field and a Checklist item check box

steps: In **Assignee**, choose who does it. Enter a due date and time.
Tick **Checklist item** for a simple tick-off item.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The task appears in the list. A progress bar shows how many tasks are done.

list: Tick a task to mark it done.
Select the pencil to edit a task.
Select the plus button on a task to add a subtask. Tasks have one level of subtasks.
Select the bin to delete a task. Deleting needs the edit tickets permission.

sections.title: Log time on a ticket
sections.intro: Log the time you spend, so contracts and costs stay accurate.
prerequisites: You need the log time permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Time** tab.

steps.caption: The **Time** tab with 30 minutes of billable remote work.
steps.alt: Time tab with totals, Hours, Minutes, Started, Activity, Notes, a Billable check box and Log time

steps: In **Started**, enter when the work started. Leave it empty for the current time.
In **Activity**, enter or choose the kind of work, such as `Remote session`.
In **Notes**, describe the work.
Keep **Billable** ticked if the customer pays for this time.
Select **Log time**.
sections.result: The entry appears under the form. The totals at the top, and the **Time** tab badge, go up.

blocks.note: Billable time uses up prepaid hours on the customer's contract. Only people allowed to see costs see **Cost** and **Billable value**. You can delete your own entries with the bin button.

sections.title: Add watchers, collaborators and specialists
sections.intro: Add people who should follow the ticket or help with it.
prerequisites: You can add or remove yourself. To add or remove others, you need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **People** tab.
In **Add a person**, choose an agent or a specialist.

steps.caption: The **People** tab with **Temporary specialist** chosen. **Access until** is required.
steps.alt: People tab with Add a person, Role and Access until fields and an Add button

steps: For a temporary specialist, enter the date and time in **Access until**.
Select **Add**.
sections.result: The person appears in the list with their role. The **People** tab badge shows how many people follow the ticket.

rows: Gets a notification about every update.
Helps with the ticket. Mentioning someone in an internal note makes them a collaborator.
Gets access to the ticket until the end date, then loses it.

blocks.tip: To watch a ticket yourself, open **More actions** and choose **Watch**. Choose **Stop watching** to stop.

sections.title: Schedule a follow-up reminder
sections.intro: Get a reminder to check back on a ticket at a set time.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Follow-ups** tab.
In **Remind at**, enter the date and time.
In **Remind**, choose who to remind. Leave it empty to remind yourself.

steps.caption: The **Follow-ups** tab with a note. **Schedule** works once **Remind at** has a value.
steps.alt: Follow-ups tab with Remind at, Remind and Note fields and a Schedule button

steps: Select **Schedule**.
sections.result: The reminder appears in the list as **Pending**. At the set time, a **Follow up on** notification arrives.

blocks.tip: Select **Cancel** next to a pending reminder to remove it.

sections.title: Lock a ticket while you work on it
sections.intro: Lock a ticket so that nobody changes it while you work on a fix.
prerequisites: You need the edit tickets permission.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Lock while I work on it**.
When you finish, open **More actions** and choose **Unlock**.
sections.result: The header shows **Locked by you**. Others see **Locked by** and your name.

list: A lock lasts 10 minutes. The message tells you when it ends.
While a ticket is locked, others cannot edit, assign, transfer, change the status or resolve it.
A lock does not block replies, notes, tags or links.
Supervisors can unlock a ticket that someone else locked. The menu item then shows the person's name.

sections.title: Mark a ticket as spam or delete it
sections.intro: Remove junk tickets from every queue. Both actions move the ticket to the recycle bin.
prerequisites: You need the delete permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.
steps: Open **More actions** and choose **Mark as spam…** or **Delete…**.
For **Delete…**, type the ticket number, such as `#1206`, to confirm.
Select **Mark as spam** or **Delete**.
sections.result: The ticket tab closes and the ticket leaves every queue.

blocks.note: After **Mark as spam**, future messages from the same sender are treated as spam. To bring a ticket back, see [Restore a deleted ticket](#tv-restore).

sections.title: The More actions menu
sections.intro: Open **More actions** (the **⋯** button in the header) for every ticket action. Greyed-out items need a permission you do not have.

blocks.caption: The **More actions** menu of an escalated, open ticket.
blocks.alt: More actions menu listing Assign, Transfer, Escalate further, Change status, Resolve, Close, Merge, Split, Clone, Link, Watch, Lock, Override entitlement, Mark as spam and Delete

rows: Assigns the ticket. See [Assign a ticket](#wt-assign).
Moves the ticket to another department. See [Transfer a ticket to another department](#wt-transfer).
Raises the escalation level. See [Escalate a ticket](#wt-escalate).
Changes the status with a comment. See [Change the status with a comment](#wt-change-status).
Resolves an open ticket, or reopens a resolved or closed one.
Closes the ticket after you confirm.
Merges duplicates into this ticket. See [Merge duplicate tickets](#wt-merge).
Moves messages to a new ticket. See [Split messages into a new ticket](#wt-split).
Creates a copy of the ticket without its conversation.
Links another ticket. See [Link related tickets](#wt-link).
Adds or removes you as a watcher at once.
**Lock while I work on it** or **Unlock**
Locks or unlocks the ticket at once. See [Lock a ticket while you work on it](#wt-lock).
Lets the team work the ticket although the customer is not entitled. It needs a reason, which is audited.
Remove the ticket from every queue. See [Mark a ticket as spam or delete it](#wt-spam-delete).

sections.title: When someone else changed the ticket
intro: Two people can change a ticket at the same time. If someone saved the ticket after you opened it, your change is not saved straight away.
Instead, the **Someone else changed this ticket** dialog opens. The ticket already shows the latest saved values.

rows: Each field you tried to change.
The value the other person saved.
The value you tried to save.

steps: Compare the two values for each field.
Select **Keep theirs** to keep the other person's values and drop your change.
Or select **Re-apply my change** to save your values over theirs.

sections.title: See who else is on the ticket
intro: Avatars at the right of the ticket header show who else has the ticket open. Point to an avatar to see the person's name and what they are doing.
A pulsing ring around an avatar means the person is typing. A banner then says, for example, **Priya Raman is writing a reply** or **is writing a note**.

blocks.tip: Before you reply, check the banner. If a colleague is already writing a reply, wait for it or add an internal note instead.

sections.title: What automation does on your tickets
intro: Your administrator sets up automation rules and blueprints. As an agent, you see what they do on your tickets.
Turn on **Activity** in the conversation to see these entries.

blocks.caption: Activity entries on a ticket. A rule raised the priority to **Critical**, added a tag and notified two agents.
blocks.alt: Conversation with activity entries from an automation rule and an AI sentiment entry

list: Rule entries name the rule, such as **Rule** and the rule name with **applied** and what it did.
Rules can assign a ticket, change its priority, add tags, add notes or send replies.
The service clock adds entries when a target is at risk or breached. It can raise the escalation level, the priority or the assignee.
The AI assistant can flag the customer's mood, such as **AI flagged the customer as frustrated**.
Blueprints guide a ticket through set steps. You run the next step on the **Blueprint** tab. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).
When a step needs approval, the request appears on the **Approvals** page. See [The Approvals page](#cc-approvals-page).

blocks.note: SupportDesk has no agent macros. Reply templates insert text only. See [Use a reply template](#rn-templates).

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts on a ticket
sections.intro: These shortcuts work while a ticket is open, but not while you type in a field. See also [Keyboard shortcuts](#gs-shortcuts).

rows: Open the composer for an internal note.
Open the next or previous ticket in the list.

troubleshooting.problem: **Ticket not found** appears when you open a ticket.
troubleshooting.cause: The ticket was deleted or merged, or it is outside what you are allowed to see.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Close tab**. Check the number. If the ticket was merged, open the ticket it was merged into.

troubleshooting.problem: The quick edit fields or menu items are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: You lack the permission, or someone else locked the ticket.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the header for **Locked by**. Wait for the lock to end, or ask a supervisor to unlock it.

troubleshooting.problem: The status you want is not in the **Status** list.
troubleshooting.cause: Your administrator limits which status can follow the current one, or the ticket follows a blueprint.
troubleshooting.fix: Move through an allowed status first, or use the **Blueprint** tab.

troubleshooting.problem: A status change shows **Some values were not accepted**.
troubleshooting.cause: A field is required for the new status, such as a vendor reference.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill in the field on the **Details** tab, select **Save**, then change the status again.

troubleshooting.cause: Your workspace requires a resolution code.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a code in **Resolution code**, then select **Resolve**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Escalate** shows **Say why the ticket needs escalating.**
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a reason, then select **Escalate** again.

troubleshooting.problem: **Reopen** shows **Say why the ticket is reopened.**
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a reason, then select **Reopen** again.

troubleshooting.problem: A transfer shows **Approval requested** and the ticket does not move.
troubleshooting.cause: The department needs a supervisor's approval for transfers.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the approval. Check its progress on the **Approvals** page.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Someone else changed this ticket** dialog opens.
troubleshooting.cause: A colleague saved the ticket after you opened it.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the values. Select **Keep theirs** or **Re-apply my change**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Split** shows **The new ticket needs a subject.**
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a subject for the new ticket, then select **Split**.

faq.q: Why do all the countdowns in the header turn red after one target is missed?
faq.a: The header countdowns use the ticket's overall SLA state. The SLA section of the context pane shows the real state of each target.

faq.q: Does the customer see that I escalated or locked a ticket?
faq.a: No. Escalations, locks, tasks, time entries and follow-ups are only visible to agents.

faq.q: What happens to a resolved ticket that nobody touches?
faq.a: It closes itself after the number of days your administrator sets. The standard is 7 days.
No. Check the tickets in the **Merge tickets** dialog before you select **Merge**.

glossary.definition: One of six fixed groups every status belongs to: Open, Assigned, In progress, Waiting, Resolved or Closed.
A finer reason inside a status, such as information requested inside Waiting on Customer.
A time limit from the SLA policy, such as first response, next response or resolution.
A number that goes up each time a ticket is escalated, by a person or by the service clock.
Moving the conversation of duplicate tickets into one ticket and closing the duplicates.
Moving some messages of a ticket into a new ticket for the same customer.
Creating a new ticket with the same customer, fields and description, but without the conversation.
A person who gets a notification about every update on a ticket.
An agent who helps with a ticket. Mentioning someone in an internal note makes them a collaborator.
A person given access to a ticket until a set end date.
A reminder to check back on a ticket at a set time.
A 10-minute hold that stops others from editing, assigning or resolving a ticket while you work on it.
The avatars in the ticket header that show who else has the ticket open and who is typing.
The right-hand pane of the ticket workspace with the customer, contact, service targets, contracts and earlier tickets.
Whether a customer's contract covers a request. The ticket header shows it as a badge.
